section: Ask MD Live Chat — Entry Flows

left.name: Summary
left.heading: Ask MD Live Chat: Entry Flows
blocks: The chat popup opens with three entry buttons. Each one is a deliberately different interaction pattern: they differ in how the conversation behaves, not only in which topic they cover.
Popular Topics  ·  Ask MD Live  ·  Ask about conditions
Picks a destination and stops there: one internal article.
Keeps the conversation going without pointing outside itself, unless the user asks for an article.
Keeps the conversation going too, but ends by sending the user to the original MD Live blog article.

left.name: Knowledgebase
left.heading: Knowledgebase
blocks: The content behind the chat comes from two repo sources. Popular Topics serves articles, Ask MD Live paraphrases them, and Ask about conditions uses blog snippets.
{{stats.categories}} article categories in public/, plus short blog snippets in conditionsFlow.ts
Markdown files grouped into {{stats.categories}} categories. Each ## heading is a question and the text under it is the answer.
{{stats.conditions}} conditions with about {{stats.snippets}} short snippets, parsed from the MD Live blog. Blog URLs are not in the repo yet.
KB_SCHEMA.json says {{stats.schemaQA}} Q&A pairs, but the article files contain {{stats.qaHeadings}} question headings.

grid.name: Journey A
grid.heading: Journey A: Popular Topics
blocks: The rigid, chip-driven path into the internal knowledge base. The same click always produces the same next step.
category chips → article card → full article
Never conversational: there is no “did you want to know about X too?” step. Content comes from the app’s public article files.

grid.name: Journey B
grid.heading: Journey B: Ask MD Live
blocks: A warm, bridging conversation modeled on the Women’s Health voice and tone example. Each turn gives a short answer and bridges to a related topic with follow-up chips.
It never auto-surfaces an article. One appears only when the user taps “Read the full article”.

grid.name: Journey C
grid.heading: Journey C: Ask about conditions
blocks: The same bridging engine, built from {{stats.conditions}} real MD Live blog conditions. It is a browsable front end over the blog, not a curated script.
Every snippet is offered as a chip. Cough / Respiratory and Headache add one nested level, and a “Read more on our blog” chip points back to the source.

grid.name: Edge Cases
grid.heading: Edge Cases
blocks: From Women’s Health, “Ask about my child’s care” offers Pediatric Care topics and hands off to the Journey A picker.
If the bot cannot answer, it says so warmly and offers the phone number 1-800-400-6354 as a way forward.
When the user is finished, the flow ends with a friendly sign-off and no further chips.

grid.name: How to read this file
grid.heading: How to read this file
blocks: Screens built from the repo’s real UI: its colors, radii, Montserrat and icons. Each shows the last turn of the chat thread.
The flow with no screens. Same steps and column positions as the UI page, so the two line up.
Content, tokens and icons come from the help-center-chat repo via the chat-journey skill.

grid.name: Open Items
grid.heading: Open Items
blocks: “Read more on our blog” is still a placeholder: the source data has no per-condition URLs yet.
The jump from the peds-bridge branch into the Journey A picker is described in a note, not drawn as an arrow.
The UI and lowfi pages are separate, so a change to one step has to be made on both.
